# Compiler IR v1

<!-- Generated by scripts/check_spec.py from docs/spec/compiler-ir.toml. Edit that file and run `python3 scripts/check_spec.py --write`. -->

This specification is the source of the adopted finite compiler-IR v1 contract. It replaces the interim design text of PR #480 for that contract. The production path specified here is accepted Lean Core, optimization and execution phases of one MidIR, a modeled LLVM module and its complete emitted LLVM bytes. Each claim identifies its required work, scoped tests or checked theorems. The implemented Lean-source compilation path and its evidence remain in Compiler architecture. The eight decisions of #749 are recorded in the properties on the foreign runtime (D1 and D7), independent semantics (D2), storage safety (D3), edition (D4), floating carriers (D5), finite constitutional claims (D6), and the native floating profile (D8). The release audit records coverage separately from this specification; no specification text grants compiler acceptance.

[Specifications](../specifications.md) defines the [claim statuses](../specifications.md#claim-statuses) and the checks. This chapter is generated from [`docs/spec/compiler-ir.toml`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/docs/spec/compiler-ir.toml).

<a id="compiler-ir.feasibility"></a>

## Feasibility before backend admission

- Property: `compiler-ir.feasibility`
- Subject: `verification and native toolchain`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.feasibility)

Before the main lowering and proof implementation, measure official-kernel reduction and nanoda checking over about 1,000 representative MidIR operations on the 16 GiB macOS reference host and Linux. Record wall time and peak memory separately for proof preparation and checking. Qualify llvm-sys 231.0.1 with LLVM 23.1.4, the pinned Lean runtime and sequential LP64 OpenBLAS 0.3.34 on both systems, recording build time, memory, disk use and binary size. A failure or an unavailable toolchain remains a blocker; changing a pin, using native evaluation as proof, or omitting a required platform does not pass the trial.

- Example: Official Lean and nanoda replay the same isolated 1,000-operation workload as one proof and in 64-operation chunks on Linux x86-64 and macOS arm64.
- Run by: `QualificationRecords.test_both_hosts_replayed_the_same_thousand_operation_exports` in [`experiments/compiler_validation/reduction/test_records.py`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/experiments/compiler_validation/reduction/test_records.py)

Claims:

- `qualification`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `QualificationRecords.test_retained_records_bind_current_fixture_and_model` in [`experiments/compiler_validation/reduction/test_records.py`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/experiments/compiler_validation/reduction/test_records.py)
    - `QualificationRecords.test_both_hosts_replayed_the_same_thousand_operation_exports` in [`experiments/compiler_validation/reduction/test_records.py`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/experiments/compiler_validation/reduction/test_records.py)
    - `QualificationRecords.test_static_abi_records_bind_both_hosts_to_the_complete_fixture` in [`experiments/compiler_validation/llvm/test_records.py`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/experiments/compiler_validation/llvm/test_records.py)
  - Note: The reduction records give wall time and peak resident memory for elaboration, Official replay, export and nanoda. Both native hosts linked LLVM 23.1.4 through llvm-sys 231.0.1 with the Lean 4.35.0 runtime and sequential LP64 OpenBLAS 0.3.34. Their target-specific inputs executed all four GEMM entry points. The native records include object and executable sizes, build-tree size and per-phase costs. At 921f386c the public compiler also matched 121 integer results, 15 heap ownership probes and four hosted exits on each platform. Production module composition and offline distribution have separate requirements. [Two-host compiler qualification](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/actions/runs/44871839008)

## One finite edition and wire route

- Property: `compiler-ir.edition`
- Subject: `source and package admission`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.edition)

The finite public profile requires package edition 2026 and the single wire schema epoch 10. Flat input and --lib input normalize to that package envelope with protected synthesized identities and original source spans. The bundled frontend and independent Lean checker must agree on that schema. Retired versions 2 through 9, an alternate flat decoder, a missing or different edition and unsupported finite grammar forms must fail closed. The existing wire cutover and manifest-edition gate do not establish the remaining finite grammar or source-to-Core correspondence obligations. The general edition grammar and Lean-native frontend remain outside this finite profile.

- Example: A package and an equivalent flat input retain their original diagnostic locations through the same checked envelope.
- Not executed: The complete finite edition and source-correspondence migration is pending.

<a id="compiler-ir.families"></a>

## One owned static function family

- Property: `compiler-ir.families`
- Subject: `function identity and assembly`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.families)

Every named function has one owned static FunctionId, a complete method set and a checked assembly revision. A singleton function, a multi-method family and a bodyless coverage contract use the same public fn model. Static calls and function values retain their selected target and specialization key. Expected return types, import order and runtime values must not choose a method. Every body, including an unused, nonwinning or out-of-domain body, remains subject to the independent checks. Structured assemble blocks lower to edit events with statement and closing-brace spans; generated loan names are deterministic and collision-free. The migration removes public generic, method and flat assembly declarations without a permanent alternate parser.

- Example: Changing an unselected method or a family owner invalidates the family evidence even if a selected call returns the same value.
- Not executed: The unified family and structured assembly migration is pending.

<a id="compiler-ir.operators"></a>

## Operator spelling preserves family identity

- Property: `compiler-ir.operators`
- Subject: `canonical scalar operations`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.operators)

Each admitted value operator selects the same canonical family, method, assembly revision, Core denotation and effects as its named call: std::operator::add, sub, neg, mul and div. In particular, / and div are two spellings of one selected operation. Nat binary subtraction remains total saturating subtraction; unary Nat negation is not admitted. Division admits only the approved static promotion pairs, including Nat/Int to Int, with homogeneous operands selecting their own division first. This does not extend division's promotion rule to other operators. Implicit represented RR/CC promotion, unimplemented bounded-integer operations, %, fdiv and unadmitted dimension-annotation forms reject. A user function with the same short name must not change a glyph's owner. All five short names denote their canonical family; a competing unqualified binding at a call or function-value site requires explicit qualification or an import alias. Naming a bounded type does not admit its arithmetic or determine its overflow policy.

- Example: For admitted Nat operands 2 and 5, subtraction returns 0; / and div retain the same selected division FunctionId and type.
- Not executed: The exact Nat/Int subset has public tests; represented scalar operations and production LLVM correspondence are pending.

<a id="compiler-ir.coverage"></a>

## Every constructor has an explicit disposition

- Property: `compiler-ir.coverage`
- Subject: `Core and storage coverage`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.coverage)

A ledger at a named source revision must enumerate every accepted Core, storage action, native storage instruction and runtime-extent constructor. For each constructor it records an admitted typed MidIR mapping or an explicit finite-profile rejection. Each admitted entry identifies its source fixture, family and method, model, ownership facts, opcode and downstream proof obligation. Any constructor or runtime change regenerates the ledger. The runtime inventory follows the transitive closure of the admitted snapshot, including frame and spectral runtimes where used; an older list of runtime modules is not a completeness argument. Missing entries must fail the coverage check instead of silently inheriting admission.

- Example: Adding a Core constructor without an admitted mapping or rejection prevents the coverage ledger from passing.
- Not executed: The source-schema guard, six instruction mappings and four structural mappings run in CI. Whole-module release coverage remains pending.

  - Note: The SSA builder appends the finite tag as one nullary instruction and resolves it in its own carrier or Hom fiber. An undeclared tag has no execution opcode. The lookup builder reads every symbol before emitting a single table instruction, preserving order and repeated references. The two phases retain the same table, argument sorts and result fiber. Reading the resolved SSA slots agrees with Core for every slot assignment, including a missing symbol or unreadable slot.   - Premises:

  - Note: For Unit, Bool, Nat and Int literals, lowering preserves preceding blocks and instructions, appends one instruction with zero operands and returns its slot. Both phases give the same value as the Core evaluator for every literal payload, environment and call resolver. An unexpected operand rejects. The compiled registry exports the four constructor identities and opcode tags for comparison with the coverage ledger.

<a id="compiler-ir.midir"></a>

## One phase-indexed typed MidIR

- Property: `compiler-ir.midir`
- Subject: `MidIR v1`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.midir)

MidIR has optimization and execution phases of the same Lean-defined Module, Function, Block, Op and Terminator representation. Typed SSA values and block arguments retain nominal model, basis and endpoint indices, FunctionId, selected method, assembly revision and specialization identity. The optimization phase retains mathematical operations and selected pullback information. The execution phase fixes the checked layouts, call ABI and resource schedule. Ordered effects are explicit; control-flow edges preserve block argument types and effect-token flow. Phase-specific well-formedness checks reject invalid dominance, missing blocks, duplicate definitions and incompatible joins. Bounded versioned dumps round-trip deterministically but carry no acceptance authority.

- Example: An SSA branch whose incoming value has a different nominal endpoint is rejected even when both values have the same storage size.
- Not executed: The pure Bool and nominal tag fragment below exercises typed branches and joins. Module-wide validation is pending.

<a id="compiler-ir.registry"></a>

## Closed opcodes have independent meanings

- Property: `compiler-ir.registry`
- Subject: `MidIR opcode registry`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.registry)

Each admitted opcode has a stable versioned tag, legal phases, operand and result types, nominal indices, independent denotation, effect or resource transition, Core origin, Opt-to-Exec obligation and external ABI where applicable. The registry covers the admitted arithmetic, indexed, storage, tensor, numerical and reverse operations. A family name alone grants no admission to another operation. Mathematical algorithm selection remains distinct from physical scheduling and profitability. An unknown opcode, unsupported attribute or unproved transformation must fail closed.

- Example: A tensor operation with a plausible shape but an unregistered dual or basis combination is rejected.
- Not executed: The closed registry and its source-to-opcode evidence are pending.

<a id="compiler-ir.semantics"></a>

## Semantics are independent of validators

- Property: `compiler-ir.semantics`
- Subject: `observational refinement`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.semantics)

The observation semantics, refinement relation and modeled LLVM semantics live in a dedicated mathlib-free namespace of VastitasOracle. They use the kernel's artifact data types but must not define meaning by the result of a validator. Observations include the selected mathematical value and pullback, ordered effects, failures, initialized storage and cleanup within the admitted fragment. Foreign operations have explicit premises. A future move into a separate mathematical package does not change these meanings or the oracle's sole local-kernel dependency for this release.

- Example: A transformation that preserves the primal value but changes the selected pullback fails its observation relation.
- Not executed: The independent semantics and stage refinement proofs are pending.

<a id="compiler-ir.storage"></a>

## Storage safety comes from checked refinement

- Property: `compiler-ir.storage`
- Subject: `ownership and initialization`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.storage)

The ownership authority is the kernel storage checker on the storage plan of accepted Core. MidIR does not introduce a competing ownership checker. Each lowering preserves the plan's initialized bytes, provenance, layouts, aliases, suspended reborrows, inside-out returns, branch joins and normal or failure cleanup through refinement. A transformation that changes allocation, reuse, aliases or release order must provide their mapping in its untrusted witness. Local SSA well-formedness alone proves none of these resource facts. No owner or loan may escape its checked scope.

- Example: Moving a release before the final read is rejected even when each function has a well-typed SSA body.
- Not executed: The checker refines linear static plans, including NativeFast GEMM, with a literal entry result. Dynamic control flow and runtime extents require additional lowering.

<a id="compiler-ir.runtime"></a>

## One foreign Lean runtime preserves exact arithmetic

- Property: `compiler-ir.runtime`
- Subject: `indexed primitives and exact integers`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.runtime)

Indexed primitives and every Nat or Int operation call one pinned foreign library built from the Lean runtime and the admitted kernel runtime modules. An operation available only as an inline C function is exposed by a fixed C shim in that library. Each call records its ABI, ownership and failure contract and implementation identity. Denotations stay the Lean definitions used by the oracle and bridge. Nat and Int remain unbounded, Nat subtraction saturates, and totalized division retains its chosen meaning. The executable must not replace them with unchecked machine-width arithmetic. Small-value inline paths need separate modeled instructions and proofs after this baseline. The Lean compiler, runtime, shim and GMP behavior remain labeled foreign premises, not consequences of the emitted-byte theorem.

- Example: An integer larger than 64 bits crosses the fixed runtime ABI without narrowing to an LLVM i64 value.
- Not executed: The LLVM-linked foreign runtime and its ABI qualification are pending.

Claims:

- `linkage`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#753](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/753)

<a id="compiler-ir.float-carrier"></a>

## Floating carriers stay in the resource layer

- Property: `compiler-ir.float-carrier`
- Subject: `numerical representations`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.float-carrier)

The four admitted representations are F32&lt;RR&gt;, F64&lt;RR&gt;, F32&lt;CC&gt; and F64&lt;CC&gt;. Each value is a resource-layer buffer with an explicit representation, component width, component count, element byte size and realization identity. Allocation, literals, maps, vectors, tensors, packing, receipts and ABI arguments retain that identity; the coefficient alone does not choose a precision. Accepted pure Core gains no floating scalar, heterogeneous product or sum for this feature. Float and SafeFloat laws are Lean reference-model statements. A public Float Monad instance, executable SafeFloat, its lift and Result-based safediv wait for the separately admitted ADT profile. F64-first is an implementation order, not permission to omit either F32 representation.

- Example: A real F32 buffer cannot be used as a real F64 buffer even when the mathematical base and dimension match.
- Not executed: Four-representation source, storage and ABI support is pending.

<a id="compiler-ir.realization"></a>

## Realization binds mathematical and numerical identities

- Property: `compiler-ir.realization`
- Subject: `realize, interpret and run`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.realization)

Canonical realize::&lt;R&gt; binds a mathematical object, its base or site, chart, dimension, representation, reference and execution profiles and revisions. interpret binds the selected computation graph; run executes through resource buffers. Affine wrappers lower to this canonical form. A real wrapper creates a fresh smooth Affine(n) object; a complex wrapper creates a fresh algebraic Affine(CC,n) object. Realizing an existing object preserves its nominal identity. Exact mathematical CC is built over RR with a selected commutative ring reduct and separate field evidence. Finite executable coordinates embed QQ(i) into CC; they do not identify QQ(i) with CC. Numerical representations have a different Kind and gain no exact Field or CommRing authority.

- Example: The canonical realization of an existing object and its documented wrapper agree only under the wrapper's explicit fresh-object and chart construction.
- Not executed: Selected mathematical affine charts have source and Core evidence. Identity realization is tested at both widths on the selected complex chart. Nonstandard chart execution and further numerical graphs remain open.

<a id="compiler-ir.native-fast"></a>

## NativeFast preserves calls and reports unavailable flags

- Property: `compiler-ir.native-fast`
- Subject: `native floating profile`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.native-fast)

The v0.1.0 native numerical profile is NativeFast. Emitted LLVM contains no floating arithmetic instruction, constrained floating operation or fast-math flag. Floating values cross it as bit patterns and adapter-call arguments. Class (i) adapters execute a fixed-order graph with separately rounded operations and are compared with the binary32 or binary64 reference; an arithmetic NaN is specified as a NaN without a fixed sign or payload. Class (ii) OpenBLAS calls are deterministic for one pinned build on one host under a foreign premise. No ideal tensor accuracy or error bound follows. Native flags are Unavailable, never empty. NativeFast does not specify the sign of a class (ii) zero or the sign and payload of a NaN from either class. Programs selecting a strict or LLVM-default floating profile reject. NativeFast is distinct from an opt-in fastfloat profile.

- Example: A program requesting observable hardware IEEE flags is rejected instead of receiving fabricated empty flags.
- Not executed: All four identity representations have public rejection, flags and storage evidence. Arithmetic adapter calls remain pending on the LLVM path.

Claims:

- `profile`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#318](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/318)
- `identity-run`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `canonical_realization_runs_into_existing_storage_and_replays_its_revision` in [`tests/numerical_realization.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/numerical_realization.rs)
    - `real32_identity_preserves_payloads_and_replays_its_precision` in [`tests/numerical_realization.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/numerical_realization.rs)
    - `complex_charts_copy_both_components_and_bind_the_full_model_chain` in [`tests/numerical_realization.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/numerical_realization.rs)
    - `reborrowed_point_restores_its_parent_only_after_release` in [`tests/numerical_realization.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/numerical_realization.rs)
  - Assumes: [Rust frontend parsing](assumptions.md#assumption.rust-frontend), [Lean-to-C toolchain and C compiler](assumptions.md#assumption.lean-to-c)
  - Note: Public check/build/run tests execute smooth real and exact complex identities at both widths through the Lean-generated executable. The receipt reports NativeFast and Unavailable flags. The source and wire tests reject a conflicting policy, precision or revision. The static LLVM resource claim covers the same four identities. Public numerical arithmetic remains pending.

<a id="compiler-ir.numeric-order"></a>

## Floating observation does not permit a compiler quotient

- Property: `compiler-ir.numeric-order`
- Subject: `fixed-order numerical operations`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.numeric-order)

The baseline preserves foreign-call identity, argument bits, effect order and returned-bit identity. A one-step NaN or signed-zero observation is not a contextual congruence and must not authorize a rewrite. A stronger rewrite needs a proved operation-closed continuation relation or a checked domain restriction. The fixed-order reference includes dot update, diagonal scale and adjoint, totalized real division and the selected same-precision complex quotient graph. Real division takes the product on an effective-zero divisor and IEEE division otherwise. Complex inverse is division of (1,+0) by its argument using that graph, without a robust fallback, implicit widening, FMA or complex-specific NaN repair. Under NativeFast, expect uses IEEE equality and a NaN literal expects a NaN; it is not a raw-bit observation.

- Example: Replacing a returned NaN's bits in a stage witness is rejected even when both results satisfy the one-step NaN observation.
- Not executed: The reference laws below concern numerical results and local flags. The stage witness checks for arithmetic rewrites remain pending.

Claims:

- `reference`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#758](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/758)
- `one-step`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.BinaryFloat`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/BinaryFloat.lean): `VastitasOracle.BinaryFloat.observe_eq_iff`, `VastitasOracle.BinaryFloat.add_one_step`, `VastitasOracle.BinaryFloat.sub_one_step`, `VastitasOracle.BinaryFloat.mul_one_step`, `VastitasOracle.BinaryFloat.realDiv_one_step`, `VastitasOracle.BinaryFloat.comparisons_one_step`, `VastitasOracle.BinaryFloat.infinity_zero_invalid`, `VastitasOracle.BinaryFloat.raw_division_separates_zeros`
  - Premises:
    - The pure binary32 or binary64 profile uses ties-to-even and gradual underflow. Each pair of real input operands consists of identical non-NaNs or two signed zeros. The arithmetic result is observed once, together with its five local flags.
  - Note: Addition, subtraction, multiplication and totalized division preserve the stated one-step observation and local flags. Equality and strict order return the same Booleans. Infinity times either zero and its totalized quotient produce an invalid NaN. Raw division of one by the two zeros produces opposite infinities. NaN results fall outside the input relation, so applying the theorem to a continuation requires further hypotheses. The validation contract requires the actual foreign calls and bits.
- `reference-boundaries`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.BinaryFloat`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/BinaryFloat.lean): `VastitasOracle.BinaryFloat.finite_realDiv_zero`, `VastitasOracle.BinaryFloat.empty_dot_preserves`, `VastitasOracle.BinaryFloat.zero_alpha_skips_inputs`, `VastitasOracle.BinaryFloat.zero_beta_skips_old`
  - Premises:
    - For real division the numerator is finite and the divisor is a signed zero in binary32 or binary64. The empty dot keeps its cell when beta tests as nonzero and one. For input independence the corresponding alpha or beta zero predicate must hold.
  - Note: A finite numerator divided by either signed zero returns zero with the exclusive-or sign and empty reference flags. An empty dot with unit beta returns the prior cell with empty flags. Zero alpha makes both inputs irrelevant, and zero beta makes the old destination irrelevant, including their contributions to flags. On 828 input tuples across both widths, scripts/check_float_kernels.py compares Lean with the independent integer and rational reference on scalar and complex result bits and local flags. It also compares C real division, ordered complex division and inverse, including aliased outputs. The C comparison checks arithmetic NaNs by class and every other result by bits. scripts/check_dot_kernel.py compares the production scalar-output GEMM adapter with Lean on 948 dots across the four representations. Its unit-beta copy cases also check the full signaling NaN payload.
- `lowering`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#751](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/751)

<a id="compiler-ir.tensor"></a>

## Tensor meaning precedes storage and GEMM

- Property: `compiler-ir.tensor`
- Subject: `finite tensor and numerical profiles`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.tensor)

The admitted rank-1, rank-2 and rank-3 finite-free Tensor model owns the meaning of Vector and Matrix aliases. A matrix tensor and a linear-map view retain their distinct dual, basis and endpoint obligations. Contraction must preserve the use of every port and its checked mathematical role; ports do not establish disjoint memory. Numerical realization is explicit. GEMM uses the pinned sequential LP64 OpenBLAS adapter for all four representations: sgemm, dgemm, cgemm and zgemm. The interleaved complex layouts have 8-byte or 16-byte elements. Pure programs link no OpenBLAS. Packing, copies, allocation, retained bytes, versions and invalidation remain explicit costs.

- Example: A 2 by 3 map followed by a 3 by 2 map requires matching nominal intermediate bases, not only matching dimensions.
- Not executed: The exact finite-free tensor aliases are pending. The public LLVM and Lean/C storage cases exercise fixed-layout GEMM in all four representations.

<a id="compiler-ir.finite-models"></a>

## Finite category models use checked tables

- Property: `compiler-ir.finite-models`
- Subject: `finite indexed families and selected models`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.finite-models)

Reusable finite carriers and tables are static data. Named category, functor, natural-transformation and Monad instances bind those data and their revisions to independently checked law evidence. Category composition covers all and only composable arrow pairs; a functor has both object and arrow maps. A selected Monad identity includes C, T, eta and mu, distinct from its proof-irrelevant IsMonad certificate. Opposite reverses endpoints and composition without duplicating the carrier. Generic finite schema checking, not the spelling std::category or a hard-coded example, supplies admission. S3 supplies a noncommuting category fixture, and the closure T(0)=T(1)=1 on 0&lt;1 supplies a nonidentity lawful Monad fixture. Derived Kleisli laws come from that same Monad evidence; its optional execution adapter owns no second mathematical semantics. The std::category::Monad schema owns the mathematical structure. The optional monad package depends on its category package. For a selected Monad M, monad::kleisli::unit at X returns eta_X. Given p from S to T X and f from X to T Y, bind(p,f) returns (mu_Y after T f) after p. The optional package exports Kleisli and KleisliTriple views of that named M. Hom&lt;K,X,Y&gt; uses the base fiber from X to T Y. extend(f) returns mu_Y after T f. compose(g,f) returns bind(f,g). lift(f) follows an ordinary arrow f by the unit at its target. Every arrow belongs to the selected category. Static object arguments select eta and mu, and the two runtime arrows of bind and compose are explicit parameters.

- Example: Two Monad structures on the same endofunctor remain different named structures when their eta or mu differs.
- Run by: `two_structures_on_one_endofunctor_select_distinct_units_and_multiplications` in [`tests/finite_monads.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/finite_monads.rs)

<a id="compiler-ir.finite-binders"></a>

## Finite binders do not admit general polymorphism

- Property: `compiler-ir.finite-binders`
- Subject: `finite table lookup and Hom indices`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.finite-binders)

The finite public forms are indexed finite carrier declarations, indexed table declarations, indexed instance declarations and ordinary fn operations. Function binders range only over statically selected finite model, object, functor, transformation, Monad and table schemas. Hom indices and associated table projections are checked independently. Input types may determine a unique binder; otherwise the call supplies it explicitly with turbofish. For M bound to a Monad schema, Obj&lt;M::category&gt; selects its objects. Hom&lt;M::category,X,M::T&lt;Y&gt;&gt; uses the selected object action. A Hom value records its category and concrete endpoints. A caller supplies the Monad explicitly because several structures can share a category and endofunctor. Checking applies T to an explicit object argument, including when T maps several inputs to the same object. Expected result types must not choose it. A dependent table signature and checked coverage preserve Hom fibers during lookup. A raw tag has no implicit cast to Hom. Runtime arrows are finite tags and lookup lowers to validated finite branches; evidence and model selection have no runtime dictionary. The 4096-key and specialization bounds remain, and finite-law work is bounded before enumeration. General type parameters, arbitrary const computation, higher-rank forms and runtime model selection remain outside this profile.

- Example: The projected composition table takes Hom(C,Y,Z) and Hom(C,X,Y) and returns Hom(C,X,Z) under the same selected C revision.
- Run by: `inferred_and_explicit_indices_select_the_same_nominal_specialization` in [`tests/finite_binders.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/finite_binders.rs)

<a id="compiler-ir.stage-validation"></a>

## Every transformation checks an untrusted witness

- Property: `compiler-ir.stage-validation`
- Subject: `translation validators`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.stage-validation)

Each validator receives the before and after artifacts plus a typed, untrusted data witness. Soundness quantifies over every witness: a true validator result implies observational refinement under the independent semantics and stated foreign premises. Separate stages cover Core-to-Opt, each enabled Opt pass, Opt-to-Exec, Exec-to-modeled LLVM and LLVM-to-bytes. The initial optional optimizations are pure exact constant folding and erasure of observationally inert metadata, each with its proof. A proposed optimization that fails validation may use only an independently revalidated baseline. A cost prediction, diagnostic receipt or cache hit is not proof. Unproved floating reassociation, FMA, NaN quotients and changes to a selected pullback must reject.

- Example: A witness preserving a function's return value but dropping an ordered effect fails the validator.
- Not executed: The stage validators and their universally quantified soundness proofs are pending.

Claims:

- `literal-comparison`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.ExactFold`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/ExactFold.lean): `VastitasOracle.ExactFold.literal_comparison_evaluates`
  - Premises:
    - The literal comparison folder returns a Boolean for two operands in the checked Core.
  - Note: For every caller environment and module, evaluation of the original comparison with sufficient fuel yields that Boolean. The fold compares two Nat literals or two Int literals at full precision. The selected and fallback methods in the literal-comparison corpus use this rule before their Boolean arguments are known.

  - Premises:
    - The closed pure MidIR opcode or function converts successfully from optimization to execution in the supplied indexed declaration environment.
  - Note: Denotation is equal for all inputs for this phase change, including branch selection, join arguments and failure. Successful module conversion preserves linked invocation at every depth for every target and argument list. Whole-module source and byte refinement with resources remains pending.

<a id="compiler-ir.composition"></a>

## Local proofs compose over the same module

- Property: `compiler-ir.composition`
- Subject: `whole-module refinement`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.composition)

A checked composition theorem joins the stage proofs across calls, selected function and model identities, ABIs, global initialization, effects, foreign calls and shared resource ownership. Function-local validation alone is insufficient. Every composed proof names the same source and environment, returned Core, phase artifacts, target, foreign contracts and final LLVM bytes. Changed declarations, negative dispatch dependencies or an ABI mismatch invalidate the relevant evidence. The global acceptance theorem has one owner and does not create a second Domain or Ownership authority.

- Example: Two individually accepted functions with incompatible caller and callee ownership conventions do not produce an accepted module.
- Not executed: The module composition theorem and its artifact-bound checks are pending.

<a id="compiler-ir.constitution"></a>

## Finite constitutional claims need their own proofs

- Property: `compiler-ir.constitution`
- Subject: `CS_fin, MS_fin and CF_fin`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.constitution)

Typed CS_fin, MS_fin and CF_fin statements range over one pinned accepted U, P, E, Q, C and evidence interface. CS_fin relates the public accepted source AST, environment and returned Core with their applicable checks. Rust parsing remains an explicit assumption where no parser theorem exists. MS_fin relates checked storage and its initialized values, loans, aliases, cleanup and failures through the modeled lowering. CF_fin connects an admitted contravariant construction to an independent mathematical denotation, including a same-endpoint noncommuting example and reversed composition. Stage refinement alone does not establish that mathematical correspondence. Official Lean proofs and axiom closure are required before finite release acceptance; broader constitutional, Spec and CInfSpec claims remain outside this statement. These are not machine-code or foreign-runtime safety proofs.

- Example: S3 arrows with different composition orders distinguish the admitted opposite interpretation from a mistaken covariant implementation.
- Run by: `inversion_uses_the_covariant_functor_checker_on_the_opposite_of_s3` in [`tests/finite_opposite.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/finite_opposite.rs)

<a id="compiler-ir.llvm-model"></a>

## The LLVM subset has explicit target and ABI semantics

- Property: `compiler-ir.llvm-model`
- Subject: `modeled LLVM`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.llvm-model)

Lean defines a bounded typed LLVM module subset with target triple, data layout, function and global signatures, instructions and external ABI contracts. MidIR block parameters become phi inputs with checked types and predecessors. Every emitted operation has a modeled meaning. Unknown instructions, floating arithmetic and unsupported attributes reject. Unproved poison or undefined-behavior promises are disabled, including nsw, nuw, exact, inbounds, nonnull, noalias, nocapture, readonly-style and fast-math attributes. Layout or disjointness facts must not enable such a promise without a separate artifact-bound theorem valid for all admitted executions. LLVMVerifyModule is a diagnostic check, not a semantic proof.

- Example: Adding inbounds to a generated address calculation without an admitted promise proof is rejected.
- Not executed: The LLVM subset, semantics and refinement validator are pending.

Claims:

- `model`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#753](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/753)

<a id="compiler-ir.llvm-bytes"></a>

## The theorem reaches every emitted LLVM byte

- Property: `compiler-ir.llvm-bytes`
- Subject: `LLVM printer, parser and handoff`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.llvm-bytes)

A deterministic Lean-defined printer and bounded parser establish the modeled module's round-trip and correspondence to its complete canonical LLVM .ll byte sequence. A checksum or AST identity alone is insufficient. Before native optimization, the driver rereads the final file, compares all bytes with the verified sequence and supplies the same immutable buffer to the in-process libLLVM parser. A Rust builder, normalization pass or parser result must not alter the verified input. A byte change, target change, parser disagreement or extra instruction fails closed. The external parser and handoff remain labeled host premises and receive adversarial tests.

- Example: Changing one byte after verification prevents native code generation even if a stored hash or theorem name remains unchanged.
- Not executed: Unary and binary lookup, the static forwarder, literal and folded integer entries, an assembled Boolean branch and closed finite package entries have complete canonical-byte theorems. General functions and release verification modes remain pending.

Its general Lean theorems establish roundtrip and arbitrary-input canonicality for those codecs, including full consumption and size bounds. This test claim does not cover instructions, functions, CFG/phi, module well-formedness, external LLVM semantics or accepted Core. <a id="compiler-ir.verification-modes"></a>

## Fast and Official verify the same artifact obligations

- Property: `compiler-ir.verification-modes`
- Subject: `compiler verification modes`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.verification-modes)

The two compiler modes are --mode=fast and --mode=official, with fast as the default. Both retain the same source, identity, ownership, stage and complete LLVM-byte obligations. Fast audits input-bound exported Lean evidence with the pinned toolchain's out-of-process nanoda_bin and reports verifier=nanoda and official_kernel_checked=false. Official checks those obligations with the pinned official Lean kernel and reports official_kernel_checked=true only after successful artifact and environment binding. Official reduction uses kernel-checked proof terms, not native_decide, bv_decide, ofReduceBool or an unproved axiom. Constitutional CI uses the official kernel only and is not a third compiler mode. A failed verifier must not silently change modes.

- Example: An export unsupported by nanoda is rejected in Fast and requires an explicit Official invocation.
- Not executed: The standalone signed-literal and live boxed-program qualifications exercise the verifier workers. General per-build verification and public mode selection remain pending.

Claims:

- `modes`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#282](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/282)
- `boxed-stage`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.BoxedCertificate`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/BoxedCertificate.lean): `VastitasOracle.BoxedCertificate.corresponds`
  - Premises:
    - The public emitter returns the checked boxed integer publication of this exact subject. The concrete execution-model certificate is valid.
  - Assumes: [Rust frontend parsing](assumptions.md#assumption.rust-frontend)
  - Note: The wire decodes to the certified ordered physical paths, offsets, texts and entry. The certified full revision equals the artifact reconstructed from the independently checked program, including dispatch winners and operator sites. The certified Int agrees with the returned Core and both MidIR stages. The parser accepts all certified bytes as the published module. Closed stage proofs and the public emitter's dependent publication witness have distinct roles. The standalone driver checks the former per input.

<a id="compiler-ir.proof-binding"></a>

## Proof binding authenticates statements and dependency closure

- Property: `compiler-ir.proof-binding`
- Subject: `proof and environment authentication`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.proof-binding)

Per-build evidence binds the source packages, edition, Charter, selected Core and MidIR, target, foreign environment and complete LLVM bytes to the theorem's type and proof. The standard axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound require their pinned statements and declaration structures, not only matching rendered names. The entire transitive declaration environment is checked, including unused disallowed axioms in an export. A versioned Fast coverage ledger identifies supported nanoda export forms; unsupported, truncated, stale, ambiguous or unbound exports reject. A standalone audit-lean result stays diagnostic and cannot authorize compilation. A cache hit or digest equality never skips the per-build semantic obligations.

- Example: An export declaring propext with a different proposition is rejected despite its matching printed name.
- Not executed: The signed-literal qualification binds a fixed complete export. The boxed-program stage verifier regenerates the declaration prefix for the current revision and checks the supplied proof of its precise proposition. A general compiler export policy and public Fast coverage ledger remain pending.

Claims:

- `authentication`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#282](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/282)

<a id="compiler-ir.check-build"></a>

## Check stops after verified LLVM IR

- Property: `compiler-ir.check-build`
- Subject: `command results and receipts`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.check-build)

check and build construct and verify the same canonical chain through the complete LLVM bytes. check stops before the libLLVM backend, object generation and linking; a check-only distribution may omit native backend linkage. build additionally performs the byte comparison, object generation, host link and atomic output installation. Receipts separate verification mode, verifier, official-kernel status, verification endpoint and native-build status. They record target, ABI, runtime and backend identities. Official acceptance means verified LLVM IR under stated premises, never verified machine code. Optional diagnostics have no semantic acceptance authority.

- Example: A successful Official check reports LLVM IR verification and no native executable, rather than a generic kernel_verified bit.
- Not executed: The opt-in LLVM preview reports a compiled checker and its artifact endpoint. Fast and Official mode qualification remain open.

Claims:

- `commands`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#417](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/417)
- `preview`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)

    - `exact_exit_status_and_library_bytes_come_from_checked_public_core` in [`tests/llvm_preview.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/llvm_preview.rs)

    - `target_choice_and_output_form_are_explicit` in [`tests/llvm_preview.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/llvm_preview.rs)
    - `every_declared_function_must_belong_to_the_preview_module` in [`tests/llvm_preview.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/llvm_preview.rs)
    - `sealed_library_revision_is_checked_on_the_complete_module` in [`tests/llvm_preview.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/llvm_preview.rs)
    - `closed_exact_operators_retain_method_keys_and_unbounded_values` in [`tests/llvm_preview.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/llvm_preview.rs)
    - `closed_constant_folding_limits_expansion_through_bindings` in [`tests/llvm_preview.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/llvm_preview.rs)

Its whole-module output covers a literal or folded integer main, a branch on a contributed Boolean method, closed finite applications with zero to six ordered lookup inputs, and a forwarding library. The checker accounts for all source functions. A sealed forwarding library checks the assembly revision and call target even when another alias yields identical bytes. The protocol records modeled-llvm-bytes, compiled-lean-checker, official_kernel_checked=false and native_generated=false. Production Fast and Official per-artifact proof checking remain pending.

<a id="compiler-ir.backend"></a>

## Native generation consumes the verified input in process

- Property: `compiler-ir.backend`
- Subject: `llvm-sys backend`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.backend)

The production native backend uses pinned llvm-sys 231.0.1 and qualified LLVM 23.1.4 libraries to parse the verified bytes and generate objects in process, followed by the platform linker. llvm-as, opt and llc may serve as diagnostics but are not mandatory production subprocesses. Missing or incompatible LLVM development libraries fail clearly in a source build; Cargo must not silently fetch another revision. Each build records library build and link identity, pass and target-machine options, CPU features, data layout and linker inputs. Backend optimization, machine code, runtime libraries and host execution remain outside the emitted-IR theorem. The driver preserves private temporaries, input/output alias protection, signal cleanup and atomic output installation without a Lean/C fallback.

- Example: A numerical build with a mismatched runtime or ABI leaves an existing output executable unchanged.
- Not executed: Source builds with the llvm-native feature use the in-process LLVM 23.1.4 adapter for closed integer and finite package entries. General runtime, numerical and distribution qualification remain pending.

Claims:

- `native`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#753](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/753)
  - Note: The [literal](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/experiments/compiler_validation/llvm/results/macos-arm64/exit-status.json) and [folded arithmetic](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/experiments/compiler_validation/llvm/results/macos-arm64/folded-arithmetic.json) entries each yielded 374 checked LLVM bytes and a 512-byte object on macOS arm64 using LLVM 23.1.4 and llvm-sys 231.0.1. The installed processes returned 255 and 10. The feature-enabled CLI regression preserves an earlier executable after link failure or rejected input and rejects overwriting the source. The [complete closure Monad run](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/experiments/compiler_validation/llvm/results/macos-arm64/finite-kleisli.json) records the linked symbols, actual 4,463 bytes, 2,760-byte object, both exit edges, and four rejected byte edits. The triple extension variant emits 5,326 bytes and a 3,176-byte object, and returns 42 on both native paths. Production verification modes, general executable modules and Linux qualification remain open.

<a id="compiler-ir.distribution"></a>

## Qualified distributions include the pinned components

- Property: `compiler-ir.distribution`
- Subject: `Linux and macOS distributions`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.distribution)

Qualified prebuilt distributions statically link LLVM where supported and include the pinned Lean checker and runtime files, the toolchain-shipped nanoda_bin, and sequential LP64 OpenBLAS 0.3.34. Numerical executables alone link OpenBLAS. Ordinary check and build use no network download or separately installed elan, Cargo or LLVM. A smaller official-checker bundle requires loader, ABI, statement, export and axiom-authenticity tests first; otherwise the required pinned toolchain subset is shipped. Source builds keep explicit LLVM development-toolchain and OpenBLAS prefix requirements. Components retain their licenses and notices. A missing or mismatched component fails explicitly; no claim of a fully static operating-system runtime follows.

- Example: An offline pure-program install smoke test links no OpenBLAS, while a numerical smoke test uses the bundled qualified library.
- Not executed: Self-contained native distributions and their offline installation tests are pending.

Claims:

- `packaging`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#753](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/753)

<a id="compiler-ir.lean-comparison"></a>

## Lean EmitLLVM is a comparison target

- Property: `compiler-ir.lean-comparison`
- Subject: `LLVM emitter comparison`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.lean-comparison)

Compare the emitter with Lean.Compiler.IR.EmitLLVM from the pinned Lean 4.35.0 source. That source records untested LLVM CI and pending IO, void parameter and static-initializer ABI updates. It builds a mutable LLVM module and writes bitcode; it is not the correctness oracle for Vastitas's canonical textual LLVM bytes. Compare signatures, control flow, runtime ownership, initialization, call order and cost on shared scalar, branch, static-call, Pair and cleanup examples. Where the Lean emitter runs, retain disassembled IR. Record unsupported examples as comparison gaps and check Vastitas against its independent proofs and C or Lean references. Do not copy unproved attributes or fixed pointer-width assumptions. Repair of the entire upstream LLVM emitter is outside this release requirement.

- Example: A join-point example compares Lean's variable slots with Vastitas's validated phi inputs without requiring byte-identical IR.
- Not executed: The generated closure package has five named calls in its entry and an explicit exit phi. The pinned Lean emitter uses slots for join arguments. The host toolchain lacks upstream bitcode emission.

Claims:

- `comparison`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#753](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/753)

<a id="compiler-ir.release-evidence"></a>

## Release evidence has separate dimensions

- Property: `compiler-ir.release-evidence`
- Subject: `finite admission and conformance`
- Rule: [Compiler IR v1](../spec/compiler-ir.md#compiler-ir.release-evidence)

The release matrix links the finite public grammar, selected identities, accepted Core, MidIR opcodes, complete LLVM bytes, proof environment and native fixtures for each mandatory row. Feature implementation, independent proof, verified emission, native testing and measured performance remain separate dimensions. The six claim statuses retain their specification meanings. A names-only bounded-integer row has no implied executable coverage. Every admitted executable family has positive and negative public fixtures and its mode-specific qualification; a specified rejection is recorded separately from a successful Fast check. Neither this matrix nor the specification is another checker, proof or release authority. Missing mandatory evidence prevents release completion.

- Example: The twelve bounded-integer names can have a completed naming contract while their LLVM and native implementation is Not claimed.
- Not executed: The release matrix and deterministic evidence rollup are pending.

Claims:

- `audit`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#755](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/755)

<a id="compiler-ir.performance"></a>

## Performance is measured outside proof claims

- Property: `compiler-ir.performance`
- Subject: `cost and compile latency`
- Rule: [Performance evidence](../storage-ownership.md#performance-evidence-and-acceptance)

Measure checking and proof preparation, LLVM code generation and linking separately from native execution. Record runtime calls, allocation, copies, packing, retained and peak bytes, and compare the full lifecycle and prepared reuse scopes with equivalent C. Match algorithms, scalar representations, layouts, backend versions, thread counts and output contracts. Acceptance timing runs in CI with the reported CPU and operating system; an interval crossing its declared budget is inconclusive. LLVM use and BLAS use alone are no C-class performance claim. The baseline passes its per-operation call costs to later validated integer fast paths, floating instructions, alias and range promises, vectorization and inlining.

- Example: A reused-buffer numerical call reports zero allocation separately from its measured overhead relative to the same plain-C call.
- Not executed: Matched measurements of the MidIR and LLVM pipeline are pending.

Claims:

- `measurement`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#753](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/753)

<a id="compiler-ir.source.acceptance"></a>

- Property: `compiler-ir.source.acceptance`
- Subject: `Finite source admission`
- Rule: [Planned LLVM compiler path](../development/architecture.md#planned-llvm-compiler-path)

The edition-2026 manifest and finite grammar use schema epoch 10 for packages and normalized single-file inputs. The Lean checker independently accepts the actual input, including the selected finite function or method, package and assembly revisions, and retains the exact Core and its checks. Both modes use that same result. The Rust frontend and any serialized IR supply candidates. The source, module and evidence stay tied to the same dependency and Charter environment. The finite source, category, tensor and exact RR/CC cases enter the release matrix with their actual acceptance and rejection evidence.

- Example: A flat file and a package each use the sole current wire schema. A forged method winner cannot grant acceptance.

<a id="compiler-ir.midir.phases"></a>

## A single typed IR has two phases

- Property: `compiler-ir.midir.phases`
- Subject: `Phase-indexed MidIR modules`
- Rule: [Planned LLVM compiler path](../development/architecture.md#planned-llvm-compiler-path)

A v1 module records its phase, admission profile, source and dependency revisions, target triple, data layout, ABI and numerical policy. The Lean representation has functions, typed SSA block parameters, operations and terminators. It retains selected body, method and assembly identities, nominal types and endpoints, and explicit control and effect ordering. Verify CFG targets, argument types, dominance and symbol resolution on actual artifacts. Optimization retains the source-selected algorithm and the mathematical facts needed for rewrites. Execution makes guards, layouts, cleanup and ABI choices explicit. Typed dumps round-trip as bounded untrusted candidates. The ownership authority is the kernel storage checker over the accepted plan. MidIR validators preserve initialization, aliases, permissions and ownership by refinement. Witnesses for allocation, alias or release changes relate both plans. Proof-only data may be erased after the checks that use it.

- Example: A join checks its block arguments and preserves the move and initialization obligations of both branches.
- Not executed: The phase-indexed constructors and their validator are pending.

Claims:

- `representation`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#750](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/750)

<a id="compiler-ir.midir.registry"></a>

## The operator registry is closed

- Property: `compiler-ir.midir.registry`
- Subject: `Admitted MidIR operations`
- Rule: [Planned LLVM compiler path](../development/architecture.md#planned-llvm-compiler-path)

The registry assigns each admitted Core and storage operation a phase, typing rule, denotation, lowering obligation and explicit result or effect contract. Publish constructor coverage against a named accepted-Core revision and regenerate it when the admitted constructors change. Unsupported operators fail admission. Tensor operations retain mathematical axes, bases, tensor versus map identity, dual and conjugation roles, and the separate storage layout. Rewrites of an admitted reverse-AD operation preserve both its primal and selected pullback. Equal dimensions do not select an identity or a method.

- Example: A contraction with equal-sized axes still rejects a mismatched nominal endpoint.
- Not executed: The closed MidIR registry and its source coverage ledger are pending.

- `registry`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)

<a id="compiler-ir.native.contract"></a>

## Numerical execution uses declared foreign calls

- Property: `compiler-ir.native.contract`
- Subject: `The NativeFast and Lean runtime premises`
- Rule: [Planned LLVM compiler path](../development/architecture.md#planned-llvm-compiler-path)

Indexed primitives and arbitrary-precision Nat and Int call one Lean-compiled runtime library under a labeled foreign premise. A C shim exposes operations that the runtime offers only inline. Each admitted Nat or Int operation is a call in this profile. Represented floating values stay in the resource layer and cross LLVM as bits and arguments to adapter calls. All four F32/RR, F64/RR, F32/CC and F64/CC representations are required. GEMM uses the pinned sequential LP64 OpenBLAS 0.3.34 adapter for sgemm, dgemm, cgemm and zgemm under a labeled host/build-specific premise, with the corresponding real or interleaved complex layout. A program that needs no numerical runtime requires no OpenBLAS. Fixed-order adapter results follow the reference result bits, with a NaN class where the reference does not specify the sign or payload. OpenBLAS results have the stated determinism premise on one pinned build and host. Error bounds and numerical correctness claims need their own evidence. The NativeFast flags observation is unavailable. Its storage expectation uses IEEE equality and a NaN expectation tests for NaN. Preserve foreign-call identity, argument bits and order even where an observation abstracts the result. The modeled LLVM subset emits no floating-point instructions and rejects strict, LLVM-default and unadmitted sign-observing profiles. Admitted division is totalized. The ordered same-precision scaled complex quotient uses totalized real divisions and fixes the order and effects of the graph, with inverse through the same graph. Emit no fallback, FMA or raw CUDA division substitution. Float values gain no public pure-Core float carrier. SafeFloat and the Result forms of safe division wait for the Result language support.

- Example: A complex GEMM lowers to the selected adapter symbol with the original layouts and arguments, while the receipt records flags as unavailable.
- Not executed: Public LLVM builds execute all four identity copies and fixed-layout matrix products. Public scalar arithmetic and the complete four native realization rows remain pending.

Claims:

- `operations`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#751](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/751)
- `realization`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#753](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/753)

<a id="compiler-ir.validation.refinement"></a>

## Each validated stage preserves the selected observations

- Property: `compiler-ir.validation.refinement`
- Subject: `Independent Lean validation`
- Rule: [Planned LLVM compiler path](../development/architecture.md#planned-llvm-compiler-path)

Define observation semantics and refinement in a dedicated namespace of the mathlib-free VastitasOracle. Its denotation uses kernel artifact types and is independent of the implementation of the validators. A stage checks a bounded, untrusted witness against the actual input and output. Prove soundness for every witness. Compose per-function checks with an independent module, symbol, call, ABI, effect and ownership check. Validate selected numerical graphs, ordering, relevant bit identity, runtime and resource premises, and the actual exact emission. A local witness that changes a caller's ABI or a wrong order of contravariant composition fails the composed check. Stage validation joins the applicable finite CS, MS and CF obligations for the same accepted source, environment, Core and evidence. It grants no other checker or proof-export path source acceptance authority.

- Example: Two locally valid functions with mismatched calling conventions fail the whole-module check.
- Not executed: Actual-artifact validation and the finite constitutional proofs are pending.

  - Issue: [#752](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/752)

<a id="compiler-ir.validation.modes"></a>

## Proof evidence binds the current build

- Property: `compiler-ir.validation.modes`
- Subject: `Fast and Official verification`
- Rule: [Planned LLVM compiler path](../development/architecture.md#planned-llvm-compiler-path)

Fast is the default and audits a Lean proof export using the matching toolchain's pinned out-of-process nanoda_bin. Official uses current-run pinned official Lean kernel replay and reduction. Both authenticate the exact source, dependency and Charter environment, Core, mid-level artifacts, complete LLVM bytes and allowed axiom closure. Unsupported export forms, stale evidence, native-evaluation shortcuts and failed internal obligations must fail closed. Constitutional CI uses only the official kernel for the language-wide claims. A successful standalone proof-export diagnostic alone does not grant a build result. Artifact caching may not waive evidence. Record mode, verifier and whether the official kernel checked the current build. Diagnostic reports and inspection commands project actual pass events, rather than supplying accepted witness data. Format errors in those reports remain diagnostic. Keep source acceptance, exact emission, external premises, native evidence and performance results visible independently.

- Example: A proof for the same function name and different LLVM bytes fails in both modes.
- Not executed: Current-artifact mode integration is pending.

Claims:

- `verification`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#752](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/752)

<a id="compiler-ir.llvm.bytes"></a>

## Validation covers the bytes supplied to LLVM

- Property: `compiler-ir.llvm.bytes`
- Subject: `Modeled LLVM emission and native handoff`
- Rule: [Planned LLVM compiler path](../development/architecture.md#planned-llvm-compiler-path)

Use an independently modeled finite LLVM subset and check the actual deterministic text by bounded parsing and exact artifact correspondence. Compare the final file with the validated complete bytes before passing those bytes to the untrusted parser. Disable unproved overflow, alias and inbounds promises and unsupported instruction forms. Fail a changed byte, ABI, target, layout or missing proof before invoking LLVM. The isolated Cargo-linked adapter uses llvm-sys 231.0.1 and qualifies LLVM 23.1.4 as the first exact native candidate on Linux and macOS. Pin the native library and link mode, runtime and adapter, pass and target-machine options, linker, triple and layout. Prefer static libLLVM linkage for supported prebuilt releases. LLVM's parser, optimizer, object emission and linker remain external premises. A Lean/C build is a separate compiler path. Record native coverage and equivalent-C timings, allocation, copies and peak memory independently of the exact-emission proof.

- Example: Changing one byte of the verified .ll file causes the final handoff to reject it.
- Not executed: The modeled emission, byte check and native handoff remain pending.

Claims:

- `emission`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#753](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/753)
